title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the handwritten notes on the divided-power de Rham complex that surround it. It is a typed page headed '- 43 -' and 'IX', stamped 361, with formulas numbered (4.3.3)–(4.3.5). It is most likely a misfiled leaf of the typescript of an SGA-style exposé IX, plausibly SGA 7 Exp. IX (Néron models and monodromy), in its discussion of a finite base field. I am not certain of this identification.

Setting.
- k is a perfect field of characteristic p, presumably an algebraic closure of F_q, with q = p^r.
- f is the automorphism of Spec(k) with f*(λ) = λ^{q^{-1}}.
- A is a commutative k-group scheme, presumably smooth and connected (semi-abelian, or abelian or affine).
- g is an automorphism of the underlying absolute scheme of A, compatible with the group law and lying over f. So g is semilinear: g*(λφ) = λ^{q^{-1}} g*(φ). Such a g is the same thing as a descent datum, i.e. an F_q-structure on A.

Claim. Let g_ℓ be the automorphism of T_ℓ(A(k)) induced by transport of structure, for ℓ ≠ p. Then:
- the coefficients of its characteristic polynomial are rational integers independent of ℓ;
- its eigenvalues are algebraic integers of absolute value q^{1/2} or q;
- for A abelian the absolute value is q^{1/2};
- for A affine (a torus) the eigenvalues are q·(roots of unity).

Proof strategy.
1. Let f_q^A be the absolute q-power Frobenius of A: identity on points, x ↦ x^q on the structure sheaf. It commutes with every morphism of schemes, lies over f_q^{Spec k} = f^{-1}, and respects the group law.
2. Hence F = f_q^A ∘ g lies over the identity of Spec k. So F is a k-endomorphism of the group scheme A, namely the relative Frobenius attached to the F_q-structure (4.3.3).
3. The transport-of-structure action on points is Γ_g(u) = g∘u∘f^{-1} (4.3.4). It coincides with F(u) (4.3.5).
4. Proof of step 3: F∘u = f_q^A∘g∘u = g∘u∘f_q^{Spec k} = g∘u∘f^{-1}, using the naturality of absolute Frobenius.
5. Hence g_ℓ = T_ℓ(F). The claim then reduces to known facts:
   - Weil's theorems on the Frobenius endomorphism of an abelian variety give rational integer characteristic-polynomial coefficients independent of ℓ, and the Riemann hypothesis |α| = q^{1/2}.
   - For a torus, Frobenius acts on T_ℓ = X_*(T) ⊗ Z_ℓ as q times a finite-order automorphism.
   - For a semi-abelian variety one uses the extension 0 → T → A → B → 0.

The page as a whole serves to compare the arithmetic Frobenius (Galois action by transport of structure) with the geometric Frobenius endomorphism, and so to deduce Weil-type statements for ℓ-adic Tate modules over finite fields.
errors: The main argument, Γ_g = F on k-points, checks out: absolute Frobenius commutes with all scheme morphisms.

The statement 'valeur absolue q^{1/2} ou q' tacitly assumes A has no unipotent part, or that the unipotent part is discarded. Unipotent groups contribute nothing to T_ℓ, so the claim is harmless. The hypotheses (connected, smooth, commutative) are not visible on this page.
Typographical slip in the original: 'peut aussi de décrire' should read 'peut aussi se décrire'.
As the 'in fact' proof stands on this page, the eigenvalue claims are not proved here. They are deferred to Weil's theorems.

ideas.what: Identification of the transport-of-structure (semilinear, arithmetic Frobenius) action on k-points with the action of the k-linear relative Frobenius endomorphism F = f_q^A ∘ g
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic vs geometric Frobenius; relative Frobenius attached to an F_q-structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Weil; Grothendieck SGA 4/5 formalism of Frobenius)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 Exp. XIV-XV (Frobenius) and, apparently, the typescript of an exposé IX §4.3 (probably SGA 7 IX); page identification unsure

ideas.what: For a semi-abelian variety over F_q: Frobenius on T_ℓ has an integral characteristic polynomial independent of ℓ, with eigenvalues of weight 1 (abelian part) or weight 2 of the form q·ζ (torus part)
ideas.modern_name: Weil bounds / weights of Frobenius on Tate modules of semi-abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX (Grothendieck), section on finite base fields (likely)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled typed page of a published SGA-style exposé, most likely SGA 7 IX, containing a standard Frobenius-comparison argument. Nothing in it is new or uncredited; the only curiosity is archival, namely its presence among the de Rham divided-power notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed, not handwritten. Header '- 43 -' and 'IX'; archive stamp '361'; pencil folio '170'.
Original text reads 'peut aussi de décrire par' (a typo for 'se décrire'); the transcription is faithful to it.
Superscripts in the first formula: λ^{q^{-1}} and λ^{p^{-r}}, correctly transcribed.
